newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps end mixed, supplies sink high sulph.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps end mixed, supplies sink high sulph.

text.p: European oil swaps ended mixed on Tuesday with crude slightly higher and fuel oil sinking under the weight of heavy supplies, traders said.

Traders waiting for further direction from the U.S. were stymied by a delay in the weekly American Petroleum Institute (API) report, pushed back to Wednesday afternoon from Tuesday due to the Martin Luther King Day public holiday.
But a rebound in crude and gasoline prices on the NYMEX underpinned swaps prices.
High sulphur fuel oil barges trimmed their losses slightly but still ended sharply lower and below the $100-a-tonne threshold.
"We're seeing the contango out toward March but just slightly," said one trader in the Netherlands.
Feb HSFO barges ended at $95/$96.50, up about $1 on the bid side from the day's low, but still down about $6 after a steep fall in Singapore prices.
March and April barges were each in about a 50-cent to $1 contango, while low sulphur cargoes were holding marginally closer to parity.
Crude values were more buoyant with weekly CFDs registering slight gains of two to six cents over the next four weeks.
This afternoon two rolls traded, one at Jan 27-31 versus Feb 13-19 at +22 cents and another of all of February against March 10-14 at +33 cents, cash traders said.
Gasoline swaps ended virtually unchanged but before a late-session rally in NYMEX gasoline futures of nearly one cent a gallon.
Northwest Europe gasoline prices have benefited from an open arbitrage to the U.S. in the last few weeks that has sucked out cargoes from a weaker local market.
Feb swaps ended steady at $214/$216 a tonne with a slight contango holding into the spring months when normal seasonal demand kicks in.
